text:
Maya: Quick thread — replay harness vs wrk showed ~2x p95 on replay. Replay is our in-prod traces replay and wrk is synthetic with long-lived conns. Any ideas?
Adrian: What's the exact QPS / concurrency + client stack?
Maya: 500 rps, 200 concurrency, target seq len 256, model=redwood-medium-int8, replay harness replays real user prefixes (lots of unique ids). Client is Go http.Client default transport, TLS enabled. Replay spawns ~1000 short-lived goroutines.
Samir: Almost certainly connection churn + TLS + small writes are killing tails. Default Go Transport MaxIdleConnsPerHost=2 => massive dial/TLS under churn. Also Nagle + delayed ACK for small token writes can add ms. Are you seeing lots of SYN/FIN?
Maya: I see many TLS handshakes in tcpdump and spikes in CPU in kernel crypto. Also KV cache miss rate high; replay sends many unique prefixes so no prefix reuse.
Adrian: For apples-to-apples you need to match client behavior. wrk usually keeps HTTP/1.1 conns alive and reuses them; replay creates many new conns. Try adjusting wrk to simulate connection churn or tune the replay to reuse connections.
Samir: Practical fixes: set Transport{MaxIdleConns:1000, MaxIdleConnsPerHost:500, IdleConnTimeout:90s}. Also set TCP_NODELAY=true on sockets if you control socket layer. For GRPC use one shared Channel (grpc.Dial once) and reuse it. Example HTTP client tweaks:
```
tr := &http.Transport{
  MaxIdleConns: 1000,
  MaxIdleConnsPerHost: 500,
  IdleConnTimeout: 90 * time.Second,
}
client := &http.Client{Transport: tr}
```
And for gRPC reuse:
```
conn, _ := grpc.Dial(target, grpc.WithTransportCredentials(creds))
// reuse conn across requests
```
Samir: If you can't set TCP_NODELAY from high-level client, try batching or coalescing small writes at the app layer to avoid Nagle delays.
Maya: Any tips on KV cache warmup?
Lina: We should seed the KV cache with top prefixes. Simple warmup: run a low-QPS sweep that visits all prefixes before the main test. Also increase batch size slightly to amortize per-request overhead; synthetic tests often use batching different from real client.
SRE Oncall: Profile dump from the failing run shows CPU hot path dominated by memcpy and repeated kernel-selection loops (we call select_kernel() per request, expensive for small batches). Client pattern forcing many tiny inferences makes kernel-selection overhead visible. Flame: https://perf.internal/fg/1778123
Samir: Also compare gRPC vs REST: gRPC (HTTP/2) multiplexes streams on one conn which helps tiny concurrent requests. But for token streaming gRPC vs REST semantics matter — test both with identical payload and streaming patterns.
Maya: I ran a quick wrk2 script that simulates churn by opening/closing connections; p95 matches replay when churn is reproduced. Good catch.
ci-bot: CI perf job #1422 — baseline p95=82ms, PR p95=164ms; tags: connection-churn kv-cold
Adrian: Action items: (1) standardize client harness to expose keepalive/pooling knobs (owner: Samir), (2) add KV warmup step to benchmark harness (owner: Lina), (3) add wrk script that can toggle churn vs multiplex modes and include in perf CI (owner: Maya), (4) investigate kernel-selection caching to avoid per-request cost (owner: SRE Oncall).
Maya: I'll run the warmup + pool fixes and post results in this thread. :thumbsup:
